sections.h2: Selling in Lubbock on a short timeline
sections.html:
A short timeline usually points to a cash buyer, while a full listing suits an owner who can wait. The choice turns on three things: the condition of the roof, plumbing and floors, any liens on the title, and how soon you need the money.

Texas Tech University, a large medical center and the farm trade give Lubbock steady demand. Near campus or a hospital, investors and renters bid alongside families, which gives even a dated house a market. The South Plains weather is hard on roofs, and inspectors and buyers look closely at hail damage and storm protection.

  • Agent listing: widest exposure, though showings, repair requests and lender timelines stretch the calendar.
  • Owner sale: skips the commission and puts pricing and paperwork on you.
  • Cash offer: quick close, no repairs, typically priced under a polished retail sale.

The Lubbock Central Appraisal District handles valuation and tax collection. Texas levies no state property tax, so your bill is the sum of local rates. Owners in the Lubbock Cooper ISD should ask the district office which rate their bill uses.

Under state law the year's tax lien attaches January 1, and a bill still unpaid on February 1 is delinquent. In a sale, the closing statement shows how the year's bill was divided.

The district's home page warns that some firms charge a one-time processing fee to file a homestead exemption. Filing costs nothing.

Owners can file for a residence homestead exemption online through the district's property search. Besides the general exemption, the district lists separate ones for disabled owners, seniors, a veteran rated 100 percent disabled and certain surviving spouses.

  • School districts across Texas subtract $140,000 from a homestead's value, and seniors or disabled owners get $60,000 more off the school levy base.
  • Counting from the year after the exemption starts, a homestead's appraised value may rise by at most 10 percent a year.
  • A senior or disabled owner can defer taxes while living in the house. The deferred debt, penalty and interest then come due 181 days after the property stops qualifying.

Questions go to 806-762-5000. An exemption does not travel with the seller, so the next occupant files a fresh application.

sections.h2: How to pay or look up taxes on a Lubbock house
sections.html:
Search the account on the district site, mail a check to P.O. Box 10568, Lubbock, TX 79408, drop it at 2109 Avenue Q, or pay online or by phone. Processing charges on card and online payments go to Certified Payments rather than the district.

Online and phone payment charges
Payment methodCharge
Electronic checkFlat fee of $1.50
Credit card2.19% of the amount paid, minimum $1.00
Debit card1% of the amount paid, minimum $1.00

The district also publishes GIS maps and takes documents and address changes by email, and the office welcomes visitors. If the title company needs a tax certificate, ask the district for one. An account that reaches tax foreclosure involves a notarized written-statement request, form 50-307, with a $10.00 fee in certified funds.

sections.h2: If you are late on the mortgage or taxes
sections.html:
Options shrink with each missed month, so move early. The lender owes you a default notice with twenty days to catch up, then an auction notice three weeks before the sale. Auctions run monthly, during daytime hours, in an area the county designates.

Back taxes work differently. On a homestead, a collector can offer a payment plan running as long as 36 months, and a written request made soon after payment may win penalty relief.

  • A sale ahead of the auction protects equity and keeps a foreclosure off your record.
  • Get the lender's payoff number in writing, and raise a short sale if the balance exceeds value.
  • Search county records for liens so nothing surprises the title company.

Both can sell fast once the paperwork is sorted. An inherited house starts with the will. Probate is possible for four years after the death, and a muniment of title can let the will and court order substitute for a full administration. If there is no will, modest estates can use a small estate affidavit. An heirship affidavit is only a sworn statement, and a buyer may refuse it.

A rented house raises timing questions. Written notice to leave is normally three days, a justice court hears the case, and possession by writ is available six days after judgment. Cash buyers often accept a tenant in place, which skips that sequence.

The Lubbock County Clerk keeps the official records. The signature needs a notary's acknowledgment first. State caps and county charges differ, so request the clerk's fee schedule. The closing agent files the deed and pays from your proceeds.

sections.h2: Preparing the house and the paperwork
sections.html:
Lubbock buyers examine roofs first, so find out the roof's age and any hail repair history, and gather receipts. Add plumbing and floor records, then check county records for liens. If a past owner left an old lien behind, learn about it before a buyer's title search does.

Ask the appraisal district at 806-762-5000 for your account summary and exemption status. Ask your lender for a payoff figure in writing. With that folder assembled, a cash buyer can give a firm number quickly, and an agent can price a listing with confidence.

The statement lists every dollar that comes out of the sale price. Expect to see the payoff on your mortgage, your share of the year's property tax, any tax certificate fee, recording charges at the county clerk and the title company's own fee. If a collector's plan or a deferral is open on the account, the amount owed shows up here too. Review it a day early and ask about anything you do not recognize.

When an offer is cash, the statement tends to be shorter, because no lender fees are included. That is one more reason a cash sale can feel simpler even when the price is a bit lower.

1. Gather the deed, the tax account details and the payoff letter.
  2. Compare a cash offer with what an agent expects to net you after repairs and commission.
  3. Select a title company and give it the account numbers.
  4. Sign before a notary.
  5. The closing agent files the deed with the Lubbock County Clerk and pays the costs from your proceeds.

A cash buyer without a lender usually closes sooner, since the wait for an appraisal and loan approval disappears.

faqs.q: Does a Lubbock house with big repair needs still sell?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer accepts the house as it sits, so an aging roof or old plumbing can stay unrepaired. Expect the offer to reflect repair cost, and set it beside an agent's listing price before you choose.

faqs.q: When do Lubbock property taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: Texas treats most unpaid taxes as delinquent on February 1, when penalty and interest begin. Statement dates are on the district's site, and you can confirm your own account by calling 806-762-5000.

faqs.q: Does filing a homestead exemption in Lubbock cost anything?
faqs.a: No. Filing any exemption is free, and the appraisal district tells owners to disregard anyone asking for a one-time processing fee.

faqs.q: Does a tax lien stop a Lubbock sale?
faqs.a: It slows things but does not stop them. A new lien attaches every January 1, and clear title waits until delinquent taxes are cleared, which the title company can do out of your proceeds.

faqs.q: Who files the deed when a Lubbock house sells?
faqs.a: The title company normally submits it to the Lubbock County Clerk. The signature must be acknowledged before a notary, and the clerk can quote the recording charges.
